narrative:
Your law school application was denied because the model predicts you have a 63.3% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. This means that, based on the available information, a majority of students with a similar profile would not pass the bar, putting you at significant academic risk in a program where bar passage is critical.

The most influential factor driving this prediction was your class standing in your third year of study. You are in the first decile, meaning the bottom ten percent of your class, whereas accepted students typically fall around the sixth decile. This tells admissions that your later law school performance remained far below the level associated with bar success. The second strongest factor was your first-year class rank, also in the first decile. Being at the bottom from the outset suggests that you struggled with foundational legal concepts, which are heavily tested on the bar exam. Together, these two indicators show a consistent pattern of difficulty that strongly outweighed other strengths.

Your undergraduate GPA, however, did not hurt you. At 3.10, it is only slightly below the average of 3.23 among accepted students and actually pulled the prediction slightly toward passing. This shows you have some academic ability, but it was not enough to overcome the repeated low rankings during law school.

If you want to pursue a legal career, focus on strengthening your academic record, perhaps by retaking courses or pursuing additional legal studies that demonstrate mastery. Also consider investing in structured bar exam preparation early, and appeal the decision while presenting any circumstances that explain your low class ranks.
